short: The UK has no AI act. AI is governed through UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, whose new automated-decision rules (Articles 22A to 22C) apply from 5 February 2026, and through sector regulators; AI policy moved to the Cabinet Office in July 2026.
title: United Kingdom AI Laws
subtitle: No AI act: UK GDPR, the new automated-decision rules and sector regulators
body_html:
Status at a glance

No AI act; privacy and sector law bind. The UK has no comprehensive AI statute and has not announced one. AI is governed through data protection law, which the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 amended with new rules on automated decision-making in force since 5 February 2026, and through the existing sector regulators. On 22 July 2026 the government announced that "responsibility for AI strategy, public sector AI adoption and the AI Security Institute will move to the Cabinet Office", with the functions of the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology redistributed. In October 2026 the AI minister named the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill as the vehicle for AI-driven cyber and loss-of-control risks; no AI bill has been introduced. Verified on 25 October 2026 against GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberPassedIn force
Data (Use and Access) Act 20252025 c. 18Royal Assent 19 June 2025In stages; s. 80, automated decision-making, from 5 February 2026 (S.I. 2026/82)
UK GDPRRegulation (EU) 2016/679 as retainedIn force
Data Protection Act 20182018 c. 12In force

Who regulates and enforces

  • Information Commissioner's Office (ICO): data protection, including the automated-decision rules.
  • Cabinet Office: AI strategy, public-sector AI adoption and the AI Security Institute, from the July 2026 machinery-of-government change.
  • AI Security Institute: renamed from the AI Safety Institute on 14 February 2025; security research, not a regulator.
  • Sector regulators such as the FCA, CMA, MHRA and Ofcom apply their own rules to AI within their remits.

Scope and reach

UK GDPR applies to controllers and processors established in the UK, wherever the processing happens, and to those outside the UK whose processing relates to offering goods or services to people in the UK or monitoring their behaviour in the UK (Art. 3(1) and (2)). The trigger is where the people are.

Core obligations

  • UK GDPR Articles 22A (automated processing and significant decisions), 22B (restrictions on automated decision-making) and 22C (safeguards), inserted by section 80 of the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.
  • The rest of UK GDPR and the DPA 2018, and each sector regulator's rulebook.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Higher-tier data protection infringementsGBP 17,500,000 or 4% of the undertaking's total annual worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year, whichever is higherDPA 2018 s. 157(5)ICO
Standard-tier infringementsGBP 8,700,000 or 2% of total annual worldwide turnover, whichever is higherDPA 2018 s. 157(6)ICO

What is coming next

  • The Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, named by the AI minister on 12 October 2026 for AI-driven cyber and loss-of-control risks.
  • The remaining commencement regulations of the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.
